tasks.title: Expired certificate
tasks.statement: The site no longer opens over HTTPS: `curl https://www.example.org/` reports “certificate has expired”. Check the expiry date on the server (`tls show`; today is 2026-10-16) and issue a new 90-day certificate for the same name from the intermediate authority PublicIntCA.
tasks.hint: On the server: `tls cert new www.example.org --issuer PublicIntCA --days 90`. The chain and versions stay as they are. Check with `openssl s_client -connect www.example.org:443`.

tasks.title: Name does not match the certificate
tasks.statement: The certificate was issued only for example.org, but users open www.example.org. The browser refuses: the name is not found among the SANs. Issue a certificate that contains both names: example.org and www.example.org.
tasks.hint: `tls cert new example.org www.example.org --issuer PublicIntCA --days 90` — the first name becomes the CN, all listed names go into the SAN.

tasks.title: The forgotten intermediate certificate
tasks.statement: The site opens for you, but clients get “unable to get local issuer certificate”. The server sends only the leaf certificate, and the client does not know PublicIntCA, which issued it: its trust store holds only the root PublicRootCA. Add the intermediate certificate to the chain the server sends.
tasks.hint: `tls chain add PublicIntCA`. The server must send the leaf and all intermediate certificates; the client already knows the root.

tasks.title: Internal certificate authority
tasks.statement: The internal service intranet.corp uses a certificate from the corporate authority CorpIntCA (its root is CorpRootCA). It is configured correctly on the server: expiry, name and chain are fine. But the root CorpRootCA is not in the PC's trust store, so the browser complains about “self-signed certificate in chain”. Add CorpRootCA to the trusted roots on the PC — this is what is done on corporate devices. Be careful: an extra root in the store is a security hole.
tasks.hint: On the PC: `trust show`, then `trust add CorpRootCA`. Check with `curl https://intranet.corp/`.

tasks.title: Old TLS version
tasks.statement: The server was configured long ago and supports only TLS 1.0 and 1.1: modern clients have disabled them and get the alert protocol version. Enable TLS 1.2 and 1.3 on the server. Then run `openssl s_client -connect www.example.org:443` and see how many round trips the handshake takes.
tasks.hint: `tls versions 1.2,1.3` — the client picks the newest common version, 1.3, and the handshake takes one round trip.
